newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund end slightly up, impact from Russia limited.
newsitem.headline: Bund end slightly up, impact from Russia limited.

text.p: German Bunds closed slightly firmer on Thursday after being knocked off their session highs by the news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked his security chief, Alexander Lebed.
Reports of political instability in Russia had weighed on the market all day but Bunds had managed to chalk up modest gains in response to firming U.S. Treasuries.

When Yeltsin announced on national television at 1400 GMT that he had sacked Lebed, the December Bund future rapidly tumbled to a session low of 99.05. The contract closed at 99.21 on the German DTB futures exchange, up six basis points.
The benchmark, 6.25 percent 10-year Bund closed at 101.44, up from Wednesday's close of 101.31. The yield was 6.03 percent.

Dealers said the news from Russia had unsettled the market but that the impact had been limited. They predicted the spotlight would shift from Russia to Friday's release of the September Ifo business climate index.

"The Iron Curtain has gone, and Germany's character as a frontline state is receding," said Lothar Hessler, bond analyst at Trinkaus & Burkhardt in Duesseldorf. "The news from Russia only has a limited impact."
Nevertheless, Bunds underperformed against Treasuries, with the spread between U.S. and German benchmarks narrowing to 60 from the prior close.
U.S. debt prices were also buoyed by a string of U.S. data, including the Philadelphia Fed index which fell to 5.3 in September versus 13.9 previously.
Analysts predicted the Ifo business climate index for western Germany would rise to 95.0-95.5 from 94.4 in August but did not expect this rise would lead to a Bund sell-off.
After Ifo, the focus would shift to German September M3, expected to be released early next week.
Remarks by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing today that M3 was unlikely to reach its four-to-seven percent target corridor this year had little impact on the market, dealers said.
After M3 growth accelerated to 8.7 percent in August from July's 8.6 percent it had become evident that M3 would not reach the target, dealers said.
But Issing said the trend towards a slowdown in M3 growth remained intact and that the Bundesbank could afford to be relaxed about M3.
